text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- About 13 million people expected to cast their votes to elect 24,253 local council members.
- Labour and social affairs ministry asks the private sector to allow employees to take time off to vote.
- Supreme court dismisses action against Privatisation Minister Abderrahmanm Saidi sued for defamation.

- Two Moroccans acquitted on appeal after serving five years of 50-year sentences imposed by Spanish court for rape. DNA analysis proves their innocence. Spaniard closely resembling one of the Moroccans has been arrested.
- Under new electoral law, fraud at polls is liable to up to five years in jail.
- United Nations Development Programme report says poverty in Morocco is more accentuated than in countries like Vietnam, Bolivia or Zimbabwe.
- Technicians at state-owned airline Royal Air Maroc protest against lay-off of 16 employees.
- James Baker, United Nations special envoy in Western Sahara, meets Moroccan Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali and Polisario Front in London in attempt to revive the peace plan.
